34.0.s.en: (1) The four sides of the new land

34.0.0.en: The land of Canaan: the land that begins after crossing the Jordan, that is, west of it. It is named after Canaan the son of Ham the son of Noah and his descendants, and the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, were known for their great wickedness.

34.0.1.en: After the tribes of Gad and Reuben, in addition to half the tribe of Manasseh, had chosen their portion east of the Jordan, which was the lands of the Midianites and Amorites, the word of God to Moses in this chapter came concerning the division of the land of Canaan among the other tribes. God declares that it is the inheritance and portion promised to His people, and makes clear the boundaries of this land, and the purpose of this was:

34.0.2.en: 1- To rouse the people not to begin their rest until they had obtained the whole land.

34.0.3.en: 2- An implicit warning to the people not to let their greed go beyond the bounds of the land that God had drawn for them.

34.1.0.en: The southern boundary begins at a point in the southeast of the Dead Sea, called the Salt Sea because of the intensity of its salinity and its lack of aquatic life, and this boundary begins going down, a little to the west, alongside the border of the Edomites (the Edomites being to their east), and this descent is to the wilderness of Zin, which in our present time represents the south of Palestine with part of the northeast of the Sinai peninsula (Map 9). The Sea of Chinnereth (the Sea of Galilee) Map (9) The boundaries of the land of Canaan

34.2.1.en: The drawing of the boundary proceeds from south of "the ascent of Akrabbim", which is south of the Dead Sea, heading west and crossing the wilderness of "Zin", and then it turns south and its end is south of Kadesh-barnea, where the people had lived much and which they knew well. The line of the boundary begins to turn toward the northwest, passing by two villages which the people also knew, lying northwest of "Kadesh", namely "Hazar-addar" and then Azmon.

34.3.0.en: Then the line of the boundary turns north toward the Mediterranean Sea, and its meeting with the sea ends at a narrow valley known as the wadi of Egypt or the river of Egypt, which is a narrow place where the waters of floods and rains gather and flow into the Mediterranean, and for this reason this river of Egypt was a seasonal river in which the water did not remain throughout the year. This river lies south of El-Arish (2 Kgs 24:7), and it is of course different from the valley of the river Nile, which lies in the middle of the land of Egypt and extends from its south to its north (Map 7).

34.4.0.en: As for the western boundary, it was easy and clear, for it is the Mediterranean Sea with all the cities or ports lying on it. Of course the name "Mediterranean" was not known at that time, and the inspired text used here the name the Great Sea, as it was also called the sea of the Philistines (Ex 23).

34.5.0.en: The northern boundary had its starting point in the west at the Mediterranean south of the Lebanese city of Tyre, and this boundary heads east crossing a range of mountains, among them "Mount Hor", which is different from the southern Mount "Hor" on which "Aaron" died, and some say that it is Mount Hermon or lies west of it.

34.6.0.en: The northern boundary continues in the direction of the entrance of the city of "Hamath", which the spies actually reached (ch. 13:21), and the line of the boundary continues to a place unknown to us now, named "Zedad".

34.7.0.en: Ziphron: a city now called "Za'farana", which lies southeast of Hamath, while "Hazar-enan" was the last meeting point between the northern boundary and the eastern boundary, and its name means the city of springs, because it was famous for its springs of water, and it lies near present-day Damascus.

34.8.0.en: As for the last boundary, the eastern, it begins in the north of course from "Hazar-enan"

34.8.1.en: and heads south to "Shepham" (unknown), then to Riblah, which lies east of the great spring of water from which the river Orontes rises, and the line of the boundary heads south until it touches the eastern shore of "the sea of Chinnereth". This sea of Chinnereth is the old name of the Sea of Galilee or the lake of Gennesaret.

34.9.0.en: The line of the boundary continues going down until it reaches the river Jordan, which represents its extension, and when the river Jordan flows into the Dead Sea, the boundary is thereby completed and closed around all the tribes.

34.10.0.en: After God had drawn the boundaries of the land for His people (the boundaries of the land of Canaan), Moses stresses to his people what God had said before, that this land must be divided by lot among the remaining nine and a half tribes, since the tribes of Gad and Reuben and half the tribe of Manasseh had possessed their land east of the Jordan.

34.11.0.en: God twice repeats that the two tribes were the ones who chose, according to the approval of their eyes, the land that belonged to the Amorites east of the Jordan and the Dead Sea. This repetition means either the confirmation that these two tribes and half the tribe of Manasseh have no place west of the Jordan, because the land of Canaan will be divided only among the remaining nine tribes and the other half-tribe of Manasseh, or that God points out that it was these two tribes who chose and not God, and consequently they are responsible for the result of their choice and its consequences, which were not good in any case (Map 10). Map (10) The locations of the tribes in Canaan

34.11.1.en: Be ambitious in your life and strive earnestly, but without greed or murmuring; that is, thank God for what you have and work faithfully, and God will bless your life as long as you feel that He is your only goal, from which you never want to be hindered.

34.12.s.en: (2) The appointment of those responsible for dividing the land

34.12.0.en: After God had set for His people the boundaries of the land on all its sides, He called them to divide it. God first chose Eleazar the priest and Joshua the son of Nun, who represent the spiritual leadership in the person of the high priest and the civil leadership in the person of Joshua the son of Nun, the disciple of Moses, and both of them served as the supreme administration of the project of dividing the land. God also commanded that ten other men share with them in the division, who were heads representing these remaining tribes, so that all might take part in and oversee the lot and the division, and no suspicion or later stumbling block might arise after the land was divided.

34.13.0.en: As usual God mentioned the name of each tribe and the name of the head or delegate for it, as a kind of record of the history of the people and also as a kind of honor to the standing of these men. Of course the first of these men was "Caleb the son of Jephunneh", known for his boldness and courage since his going to spy out the land about forty years before, who alone with Joshua the son of Nun encouraged the people, unlike the other ten spies. After listing the names of the other nine heads, God again reminds His people (v. 29) that these are the ones chosen to divide the land of Canaan among the remaining tribes. It is noted that the tribe of Levi was not given a division of the land like the rest of the tribes because it was devoted to the service of God and took only cities to dwell in, which God will specify in the next chapter. The number of the tribes among whom the land was divided returns to twelve because Joseph came to have two portions, that is, two tribes, Ephraim and Manasseh.

34.13.1.en: God in His love cares for the affairs of our temporal and earthly life and apportions to every person on earth a place and a work, ... but the most important thing God has set apart for us is the inheritance and portion of eternal life, so do not let the earth distract you lest you lose your heavenly portion.

34.13.2.en: The cities of the Levites, the refuge, and the sin of murder

35.0.s.en: (1) The assignment of the cities of the Levites

35.0.0.en: This speech was one of the last that God spoke with Moses, and it was in "the plains of Moab" east of the Jordan, a short time before the death of Moses.

35.1.0.en: The subject and substance of this speech concerned the Levites, the servants of the house of God, since they had no portion of land to possess like the rest of the tribes. So God commanded the people to give from their lands that they would possess portions, "cities", for the Levites to dwell in, with areas of the land surrounding these cities so that the Levites might raise and tend their cattle. These areas surrounding the cities were called "suburbs".

35.2.0.en: So that God would not leave to the tribes the choosing of the areas for the cities of the Levites, lest injustice fall on them, God Himself set this area surrounding each of their cities, and they are fixed areas. To make clear the idea of the division, we see that God set a first area adjoining the city, consisting of a thousand cubits on the four sides, followed by a second area of two thousand cubits on the four sides also. The first area, adjoining the city, which was the smaller area, was used as dwellings for the servants and pens for the cattle, while the next area, the larger one (two thousand cubits on each side), consisted of pastures for grazing cattle or land fit for cultivation, provided that the Levites did not work in it with their own hands but the servants or hired workers did, because the Levites were set apart and consecrated for the service of the tabernacle of meeting.

35.2.1.en: We can sum up the area of the suburbs around the cities as 3000 cubits surrounding the city on every side) ... figure 2) 2000 cubits 1000 cubits 2000 cubits cubit the city the first section 2000 cubits the pastures and agricultural land (the second section) (figure 2) an illustrative drawing of one of the cities of the Levites

35.2.2.en: Notice with me, beloved, God's fatherly care for His servants who serve Him. He does not leave them at the mercy of the tribes, but just as He had set for them their portion from the tithes of the tribes, so He also sets for them their portion of the lands; and it is a generous setting, which did not include houses only but inner boundaries and outer boundaries for each of their cities!!!.. You are great, O God, in Your giving and Your care for Your servants and the ordering of the affairs of their lives.

35.3.0.en: God fixed the number of the cities of the Levites at forty-eight cities, to be given by the twelve tribes, and then God excepted from these cities six cities which He called cities of refuge, which will be spoken of in detail in (vv. 11, 12).

35.4.0.en: God did not bind the tribes to make the proportions of the cities they gave equal, because the areas of the lands themselves were not equal, but God laid down the general rule for the division and left the detail to the heads and elders of the tribes. The rule was "from the many ye shall give many, but from the few ye shall give few", that is, whoever had a wider portion of the land would give a larger number of cities, and whoever had a small land would give fewer cities, but no tribe was excepted from giving, because these cities are given "of the possession of the children of Israel", that is, all the tribes must take part in the giving. Joshua indeed carried this out and gave the Levites the forty-eight cities; see Josh 21.

35.4.1.en: The giving of the cities of the Levites in the midst of the children of Israel has reasons, which are:

35.4.2.en: 1- So that the tribe of Levi and the rest of the tribes might feel that they were giving a tribe from among themselves to the service of God, and so obtain God's blessing in their lives.

35.4.3.en: 2- The dwelling of the Levites among the tribes gives them the opportunity to teach them the laws of God.

35.4.4.en: 3- The fulfillment of Jacob's prophecy to his son Levi that he would divide him among the tribes (Gen 49:7).

35.5.0.en: These two verses are an introduction to God's following speech about the cities of refuge. God began His speech with preparation, since they were crossing over, that is, they would cross the river Jordan and possess the promised land, and consequently they had to do what He would command (Map 11). Golan Ramoth Map (11) The cities of refuge

35.6.0.en: God had already specified in (v. 6) that the number of the cities of refuge was six cities, but here God explains to the people the purpose of these cities, which is that they be cities of shelter and protection to which the unwitting slayer may flee, who is one who killed someone by mistake or without intention or evil design.

35.7.0.en: The avenger: the nearest relative of the slain, who has the right to demand his blood in order to take vengeance on the slayer.

35.7.1.en: The slayer enjoys protection inside the cities of refuge, and the "avenger" cannot do anything to him or take vengeance on him. The slayer's stay in the cities of refuge is not a permanent stay but for a period of time that precedes his trial before the congregation, that is, as we now say, a custody that precedes the trial. The congregation that tried him usually consisted of the heads of the people and the priests, the keepers of the Law and its judgments.

35.8.0.en: God again reminds the people that they are six cities of refuge (v. 6), but He adds here that three of them are to be east of the river Jordan, that is, beyond the Jordan, and three others west of the Jordan, distributed over the land of Canaan, and the names of these cities were mentioned in (Josh 20:7, 8). The purpose of this is the distribution of the cities of refuge and their not being concentrated in one region, so that they would be spread out and the slayer could flee to the nearest available city of refuge. The longest distance in any tribe to one of the cities of refuge was thirty miles, which the slayer could cover in half a day, and there were signs at the crossroads to guide to these cities.

35.9.0.en: God makes clear that the right of protection for the unwitting slayer is not limited to the Jews but extends also to the stranger who is not of the people and who was, for example, passing through the land and by mistake killed a Jew. This right also included the sojourners, who are those who live among the people, such as slaves or free strangers, but who were allowed to dwell among the tribes.

35.9.2.en: (1) God chose the cities of refuge in the midst of the cities of the priests and Levites so that the slayer might be in a spiritual atmosphere that reassures him and calms his anxiety and fears, and there would be an opportunity for guidance and spiritual work with this soul.

35.9.3.en: (2) The opportunity is given to all, for God protects the stranger and the sojourner also from the avenger's desire for vengeance so that justice and judgment may be carried out through the heads of the congregation and its priests. His love is for all and His justice is universal, and for this reason one of the Church's beloved titles in describing God is the word "lover of mankind", since His love and redemption included the whole world according to His purpose and will.

35.9.4.en: (3) It shows the value of the human soul in God's sight and His care to preserve it in the cities of refuge. (4) His giving the sinner an opportunity to repent, namely the unwitting slayer.

35.9.5.en: (5) The cities of refuge signify the Church, to which the sinner flees to confess and partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord, and so finds his life and saves his soul from death.

35.9.6.en: (6) The avenger who demands the blood of the slain signifies Christ, who defends us against Satan and rescued us from his hand by the redemption accomplished on the Cross.

35.9.7.en: (7) The unwitting slayer's flight to the cities of refuge to save his life from death signifies a person's flight from sin and all its sources that cause his death.

35.9.8.en: When you sin, flee quickly to God in prayer and repentance before your father of confession, and you find your life and the devil cannot seize you, but you live at ease and rejoice in being in the hands of God.

35.10.s.en: (3) The distinction between murder and manslaughter

35.10.0.en: These three verses contain one repeated word, "smite", which means the present will to strike, regardless of whether the instrument is iron, stone or heavy wood ... But as long as the killing was done with will and awareness, the charge was plainly that he is a "murderer", and the punishment more plain and severe: "shall be put to death".

35.11.0.en: This verse makes clear who carries out the sentence of death on the murderer, namely the avenger who demands the blood of his slain relative. It is noted that the avenger could not kill until it was confirmed, whether by the testimony of witnesses or by the judgment of the congregation affirming the murderer's crime. The custom ran that if the murderer was tried and his intent proved, either the congregation would kill him by stoning or the avenger would kill him himself, since God allowed him this right.

35.12.0.en: These two verses present other forms of willful killing without the use of instruments of killing, which are either killing by pushing in hatred and fierceness from a high place so that he fell and died, or striking him with his bare hand but so hard a blow that it killed the other. His charge is also willful murder, and the retribution from him is like the preceding (v. 19), because he killed out of malice, enmity and anger.

35.13.0.en: As for the case of accidental killing, that is, not deliberate and without feelings of enmity, malice or vengeance, though its forms differ, whether by a mistaken push without intent to harm, or by throwing something without intention, or dropping a heavy stone without seeing so that it fell on him and he died, the slayer in this case has another ruling, unlike the willful murderer, regarding whom God had already permitted the avenger the right to take vengeance on the slayer and kill him. This is killing by mistake and it has other rulings.

35.14.0.en: God first gave the judgment to the congregation, the heads, and not to the avenger, whose mind may be absent and who may be ruled by feelings of vengeance, whereas the congregation is of course neutral and judges according to the Law. It was customary that whoever killed a person by mistake and without intent would flee to the nearest city of refuge on his way and tell the Levites and priests what he had done, and they would receive him in the city and provide him protection from the avenger of blood. This stay was temporary and was followed by his trial before the heads of the congregation. If the congregation was assured that the killing was by mistake and that no harm to another person had been repeated by him, that is, they were assured he had no hatred of the slain, he was given the right of refuge and residence in the city. God also set the length of his stay in the city until the death of the anointed high priest, and in the case of the death of the high priest the slayer was permitted to return to his city.

35.14.1.en: The unintentional slayer's remaining until the death of the high priest has reasons, which are:

35.14.2.en: 1- A punishment for the slayer for his carelessness and lack of attention.

35.14.3.en: 2- An opportunity to calm the feelings of the family of the slain.

35.14.4.en: 3- The high priest prays and offers sacrifices for the slayer, so his death is a sign of the completion of the prayer for him, and he is permitted freedom.

35.14.5.en: And this signifies the death of Christ, our High Priest, and by His death we obtain freedom from sin.

35.15.0.en: God continues the discussion of this law and affirms that as long as the slayer is inside the city of refuge, he enjoys protection, but if he goes out of it before the death of the high priest, and the avenger finds him and kills him, nothing is on the avenger, since the slayer who had the protection of the city of refuge is the one who left this protection and this right which God had granted him.

35.16.0.en: This verse is a repetition and confirmation of what came in verse (25), that the length of the stay in the city of refuge is until the end of the life of the great priest, that is, the high priest, by whose death the slayer is permitted to return to his home and his land.

35.16.1.en: God's mercy is clear in rescuing the unwitting slayer. In His love God seeks excuses for you to lead you to repentance and the correction of your mistakes and to care in all your conduct.

35.17.s.en: (4) The punishment for the crime of willful murder

35.17.0.en: In the coming verses and to the end of the chapter, God speaks of the rulings to be followed with one who has killed willfully. God began His speech by saying that what He is saying to the people here are commandments that must be carried out for all the coming generations, wherever the people dwell, that is, in all its tribes and all its lands.

35.18.0.en: God specifies two things here. The first is the duty of putting the willful slayer to death, and the second is the necessity of there being at least two witnesses to convict the slayer, because of the gravity of the sentence of killing a person, so it is not possible to be content with one witness, who may be moved by hatred to bear false witness.

35.19.0.en: God also forbids the permissibility of taking a material ransom in place of the soul that was killed, for the human soul is the most precious thing in God's creation and cannot be redeemed by anything but blood. This reminds us, beloved, of the redemption of the Lord Jesus for us, for He gave Himself and shed His pure blood to take away our iniquity from us, when we deserved the sentence of death for our sins.

35.20.0.en: God forbids the acceptance of a bribe that the willful slayer might offer so that the Levites and priests would consider him one of those entitled to the right of refuge in the cities of refuge, and that he might spend a period of time after which he would return to his house and land, for God gave this right only in the case of accidental killing. God's mercies must not be used in the wrong place.

35.21.0.en: Blood defileth the land: it prevents God's dwelling and presence among His people.

35.21.1.en: God warns the people against laxity in carrying out with all exactness the laws He commanded, affirming that silence over the blood of a dead man is an ugly thing that defiles the whole people before His eyes and withholds blessing and divine help from them, and God allows nothing but blood as compensation and atonement for blood that has been shed.

35.22.0.en: God again affirms that He does not accept that the land be defiled and become unclean before Him through the people's laxity in demanding the blood of the slayer in place of the blood of the slain, and He reminds them that He is the God dwelling in their midst, and accordingly He must be obeyed and the people must act on His commandment and orders and not be lax in them.

35.22.1.en: Be careful in your dealings with others, and do not hurt a person's feelings with wounding words or bad behavior, which they call moral killing, but be compassionate toward others, even those who wrong you, so that you pray for them and seek excuses for them.

35.22.2.en: The inheritance of the daughters of Zelophehad
